newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Bosnia mediator Bildt in hospital with infection. [CORRECTED 22:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bosnia mediator Bildt in hospital with infection. [CORRECTED 22:20 GMT]

text.p: Swedish politician Carl Bildt, who is overseeing international peace efforts in Bosnia, was in a Stockholm hospital on Sunday being treated for a suspected viral infection, a hospital spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman said Bildt, 47, was admitted to Danderyds Hospital in the Swedish capital's northern suburbs on Saturday.
"He is being treated in the Department of Infectious Diseases...for a suspected viral infection," she told Reuters.
It was unclear how long he would remain there and no further details were available.

Bildt, the leader of Sweden's oppositon conservative party, the Moderates, and a former Swedish prime minister, was taken to hospital after collapsing at his Stockholm home, complaining of a headache, tiredness and having difficulty speaking.
Bildt returned to Stockholm on Friday to visit his family.
He was due to go to London on Sunday and return to Bosnia on Tuesday but these plans were now up in the air.
Colum Murphy of Bildt's office in Sarajevo said that Bildt's illness would not affect the running of the office.
"A couple of meetings will be changed but the programme will continue as usual," Murphy told the Swedish news agency TT.

Murphy said he did not expect Bildt to be away for long as several people in the office had recently suffered a bad bout of influenza, reporting similar symptoms to Bildt, but were back at work within a few days.
"He's had this (bug) for about a week now but has continued working. As he is physically in very good shape I think it'll only be a few days before he's back again," Murphy said.
Bildt became Sweden's first conservative prime minister in 61 years after winning the 1991 general election.
(Corrects manner in which Bildt came to power)
But after the Social Democrats regained power in a 1994 general election, Bildt took on the Bosnian mission. He has earned international respect as the major powers' High Representative in Bosnia.
Bildt has said that he will give up his position in Bosnia and return to Sweden around May this year to lead the Moderates into the next general election in September 1998.
